summary: AE + SE walkthrough of Redwood Console tracing, request logs, and error analysis. Customer concerned about latency spikes and debugging flows for their multi-tenant inference service. Agreement to run a pilot and share security docs; SE to run targeted tracing queries and request logs export during pilot.
transcript:
[00:00] Maya (AE): Hey everyone thanks for joining, we're Maya Chen from Redwood, I'm the AE on your account. Luca from our infra SE team is here as well. Quick intro?
[00:10] Jordan (Catalyst): Jordan Lee, CTO. Priya, Mark here. We're excited to see the Console tracing and error flow. We've been hitting latency spikes during peak batch scoring.
[00:22] Maya: Great, high level we'll show tracing, request logs, and how to pivot from an alert to a root cause in the Console. Luca will do the deep demo.
[00:30] Luca (SE): Hi all. Quick note: I'll show both hosted and Dedicated screenshots, and some examples of the trace timeline and KV cache flags. Please stop me with questions.
[00:40] Priya: Sounds good. Our main questions: how do we correlate tokens-per-request with latency? And how to debug tail latency?
[00:48] Luca: Good. So on the Console you have a per-route dashboard, token and latency histograms; tracing is request-level so you can click a row in request logs and open a trace flame chart.
[01:05] [Luca screen share - console] Luca: Here's a sample trace, you can see stages: receive -> routing -> model-inference -> postprocess. In model-inference we break out kernel selection and KV cache hits. Note sometimes transcribed labels show K V cash instead of KV cache in older transcripts, ignore that.
[01:30] Jordan: Can you show an example where KV cache causes variability?
[01:35] Luca: Sure. Expand this trace: when prefix matches KV cache hit rate drops model-inference by ~60ms. When prefix miss we see full decode and longer kernel warmup. You can filter traces by tags: model_variant, quantization_profile, and region.
[01:55] Mark: Do we get the full prompt text in request logs? We need to redact PII.
[02:01] Maya: By default request logs show hashed prompt snippets; you control retention & redaction settings in the Security panel. For Private deployments we support customer KMS and no-logs modes.
[02:12] Priya: How do traces look when we use batching? We're planning to enable batching to reduce cost but worried about increased p99.
[02:20] Luca: Good question — Console trace shows batch composition metadata: batch size, batch latency and per-token timing. You can correlate batching windows with tail latency. We also expose a batch policy simulator in Optimize that estimates cost vs p99 impact.
[02:38] Jordan: Is there an easy way to run an A/B where half traffic goes to hosted and half to Dedicated?
[02:44] Maya: Yes, rollouts support canary and weighted splits and you can route by policy. Our Console traces will annotate which pool served the request.
[02:52] [03:00] Luca: Now I'll trigger a live example trace from our demo tenant. Notice the trace timeline: you'll see a long tail in kernel selection when the sequence length spikes; that's often a hidden cost.
[03:20] Priya: Can we export traces for offline analysis?
[03:24] Luca: Yes, there's an export API and CSV/JSON downloads for both request logs and traces. We recommend exporting the trace IDs and sampling a set for deeper profiling.
[03:33] Jordan: Security: we need SOC2+/ISO, audit logs, and SSO.
[03:38] Maya: We're SOC 2 Type II and have ISO roadmap; I'll send the security pack. Console has audit logs for role changes and API keys. SSO/SAML + SCIM provisioning is supported.
[03:52] Mark: A few demo rough edges: I've seen the Console sometimes show generic error codes. How do we map those to root cause?
[03:58] Luca: Good call. In request logs each request has an error_code and a detailed error_message. The trace will show the failing stage. For example a 5xx during model-inference can be traced to OOM on a specific model_variant; we expose GPU memory usage hints in the trace. Sometimes transcription will show model names slightly off (e.g., \"red wood-bert\"), but the IDs are exact in the UI.
[04:22] Priya: Can you demo filtering by latency window and customer id so we can debug a tenant-specific spike?
[04:28] Luca: Yep. Filter by customer_tag or route, set latency > 200ms, then apply timeframe. You get the list of request rows and can open traces. You can also pin the row to compare multiple traces side-by-side.
[04:40] [05:00] Maya: One common flow: alert triggers in Redwood Monitor, you jump to request logs filtered by alert tags, then open highest-latency trace to identify whether it's routing, queueing, model-inference or postprocess.
[05:15] Jordan: About retention and cost - storing full traces for 90 days will be expensive. What do teams do?
[05:21] Luca: We have sampling and adaptive retention: keep full detail for error traces and top percentile, and aggregated histograms for everything else. Optimize will recommend sampling rates based on your traffic pattern and SLOs.
[05:36] Priya: Any known issues with OpenTelemetry exports? We're trying to tie Redwood traces into our APM.
transcript_continued:
[05:45] Luca: We support OpenTelemetry and have an exporter; note that names might map differently so we recommend using our trace IDs.
[05:52] Priya: For pilot, we want to run a 48-hour test with 10k reqs/day and compare hosted vs Dedicated. Can SE run targeted trace captures?
[06:00] Luca: Yes, I can deploy a higher-sampling policy on your pilot routes and capture full traces for the 48-hour window; I'll share the export.
[06:10] Jordan: How do we instrument custom metrics? For example prompt size distribution.
[06:16] Luca: You can push custom tags with each request, and we index them for filtering. Also you can ingest app metrics via Prometheus integration; Console ties them together.
[06:26] Mark: Any limitations on private / on-prem deployments around tracing?
[06:31] Maya: Private supports the full Console but with a customer-controlled control plane; telemetry can be forwarded to your internal collectors. For air-gapped we ship an on-prem console bundle.
[06:45] Priya: Is there a way to anonymize prompts but keep enough signal to debug?
[06:49] Luca: Yes, we support regex redaction and token hashing. We also have a \"prompt fingerprint\" feature that preserves length and token-level stats without the raw text.
[06:58] Jordan: Ok next steps?
[07:02] Maya: Recap: we'll send pricing for Dedicated + mixed routing options, Luca will share tracing runbook and sample export queries, and we'll schedule a pilot starting ~2025-10-20 pending your traffic profile.
[07:15] Priya: Thanks, and please include the steps for increasing sampling and lowering retention during the pilot.
[07:20] Luca: Will do.
[07:22] Maya: Thanks everyone, we'll follow up with the packs.
[07:25] [Call ends]
notes: Demo included live trace showing kernel selection and KV cache hit/miss timing
Customer concerned about tail latency and storage costs for traces
Action: SE to increase sampling during pilot and export traces for offline profiling
